transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Hi, doctor. Thanks for seeing me. I guess the main thing is… I’m having a really hard time keeping my mind on a task long enough to actually finish it. I work in computer support, and even when it’s something important, like tracing a client’s network problem, I’ll look up and realize ten minutes have gone by and I’ve read the same log entries three times and still don’t really know what they said.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it’s been getting in the way enough that I thought I should ask for help.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble staying seated, especially when you're trying to focus on something?

Yes… I mean, not in a dramatic way, I don’t think, but I do notice it. If I’m sitting with a client, or even at a chess meeting, my leg will be bouncing under the table, or I’ll be clicking a pen without realizing it.

Sometimes I’ll have something small in my hands, like a cable tie, and I’ll just keep turning it over and over until someone sort of gives me that look. It’s a little embarrassing, honestly. I try to stop when I notice.
Do you also find it hard to focus or sit still in situations outside of work, like when you're at home trying to relax or during social activities?

Yes, I suppose it does happen outside work too. I don’t want to overstate it, but even quiet things that should be relaxing are hard for me to just… stay with.

Like if I’m reading a manual at home, or watching a movie with my wife, I’ll last a few minutes and then I’m making little comments, checking my phone, or getting up for no real reason. I’ve even tried those breathing exercises, and I know they’re supposed to be calming, but I end up restless pretty quickly. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Looking back, did you have similar difficulties with focus or restlessness when you were a child, like in school or during activities with friends?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I did fine enough in school, so I don’t want to make it sound like I was a terrible student or anything.

But my mother still jokes about my grade school report cards saying things like, “bright, but doesn’t stay in his seat,” or that I’d blurt out answers. And apparently I lost homework even when I’d actually done it, which is… a little embarrassing to admit at my age. But yes, that was there back then too, I guess.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through, like interrupting others during conversations or making sudden decisions without considering the consequences?

Yes… I do, though I don’t like to think of it as rude exactly. It’s more like the answer jumps into my head and I start talking before I’ve really let the other person finish.

It happens especially in technical conversations. Someone will be explaining a computer problem, and I’ll cut in because I think I already know where it’s going. Sometimes I’ll even reach for the keyboard or start doing something before they’ve finished describing it. I know better, and I do try not to, but in the moment it feels almost automatic.

I realize that probably comes across badly sometimes. Is that the sort of impulsive thing you mean?
Have you been feeling down, losing interest in things you usually enjoy, or getting irritated more easily lately?

I’m not sure I’d say “down,” exactly. I mean, I get frustrated with myself sometimes, and maybe a bit irritable when I can’t settle into something, but I haven’t really thought of it as losing interest in things or being depressed.

My wife might have a better read on whether I seem more short-tempered lately, but from my side… I don’t think that’s the main issue. Is that helpful?

Can you think of a time when you weren’t at work or at home, like when you were out in public or at an event, where these issues with focus or restlessness came up and might have affected how you were able to participate?

Yes, I suppose so. It’s not usually dramatic, but… if I’m sitting with a client, or even at a chess meeting, I notice I’m almost always doing something with my hands or legs.

My leg will be bouncing under the table, or I’ll be clicking a pen without realizing it. Sometimes I’ll sit there turning a cable tie or something small in my fingers over and over until someone gives me that look, and then I realize I’m doing it.

I can still participate, mostly, but I’m sure it’s distracting to other people. I don’t mean to be irritating. Is that the kind of situation you’re asking about?

Have you noticed these symptoms of inattention, restlessness, or impulsivity in settings beyond work, home, and social gatherings — for example, while running errands, commuting, or in public spaces like restaurants or stores?

Yes… I think waiting is probably where I notice it most outside the usual settings. Not in a dramatic way, I hope, but if I’m on hold with a vendor or sitting in a clinic waiting area, I get very antsy.

I’ll be checking the time over and over, sighing more than I mean to, or sort of trying to move things along before it’s really my turn. I don’t usually intend to be pushy, but I can feel myself wanting the situation to hurry up, and it’s uncomfortable — like I want to crawl out of my skin a bit.

That’s probably the kind of thing you mean, right?
Have these symptoms caused any noticeable problems in your relationships, job performance, or other important areas of your life?

Yes… unfortunately, I think they have. I don’t like saying it that way, because I do try hard and I don’t want to sound like I’m making excuses.

But since I lost the structure I had in my old job, things have slipped more than I’d like. My reputation has taken a real hit. I’ve lost some freelance clients because people weren’t confident I’d follow through, and there was a senior service-manager role I missed out on too.

And at home, my wife and I have had to worry about money more than we should, partly because I haven’t been as reliable as people need me to be. That’s probably the part I feel most embarrassed about. Does that answer what you mean by impairment?
Have you noticed these symptoms of inattention, restlessness, or impulsivity in other situations, such as while driving, during medical appointments, or while engaging in hobbies?

Yes, I think so… more with hobbies or things that are supposed to be relaxing. I wouldn’t want to overstate it, but quiet activities are hard for me to stick with.

Like if I’m reading a technical manual, or even just trying to watch a movie with my wife, after a few minutes I’ll start making little comments, or checking my phone, or I’ll get up for no real reason. And I’ve tried those breathing exercises people recommend, but I don’t last very long before I’m fidgeting or thinking, “Right, what now?”

It’s embarrassing, because those are simple things, really. But yes, that does happen. Is that the kind of situation you mean?
Have you noticed these symptoms occurring in other specific situations, such as while driving, during medical appointments, or when trying to focus on a task that isn’t work-related?

Yes… I think the main thing is when I’m trying to focus on something that isn’t necessarily “work” in the formal sense, but still matters. Or even with work-like tasks outside the usual structure.

What really brings me in, honestly, is that I just can’t seem to keep my mind on a task long enough to finish it anymore. I’ll be trying to trace a client’s network problem, for example, and ten minutes later I realize I’ve reread the same log entries three times and still don’t actually know what they say.

It feels ridiculous to admit, because I’m not trying to avoid it and I know it’s important. I’m sitting there, looking at the screen, but it just doesn’t go in. Is that the sort of thing you’re asking about?
Have you noticed these symptoms occurring specifically while driving or during medical appointments?

During medical appointments, yes… not so much in a dramatic way, I hope, but when I’m sitting in the waiting room or waiting for my turn, I get really uncomfortable.

I’ll keep checking the time, shifting around, sighing without meaning to, and I sometimes catch myself wanting to push things along before it’s really my turn. Same sort of thing if I’m on hold with a vendor. It’s like I’m trying to be patient, but inside I feel like I’m crawling out of my skin.

With driving, I’m not sure I’ve noticed it in the same clear way. But with waiting in queues or appointments, yes, that definitely happens. Does that help?
Have you noticed any difficulties with staying focused, feeling restless, or acting impulsively while driving or in situations where you need to maintain attention for a long period of time?

Yes… especially in situations where I have to maintain attention for a long stretch.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it’s actually one of the main reasons I’m here. I can be trying to trace a client’s network problem, something important, and after ten minutes I realize I’ve reread the same log entries three times and I still don’t really know what they say. I’m sitting there trying, but my mind just won’t stay with it long enough to finish properly.

Driving specifically, I’m less sure how to answer. But with sustained focus, yes, that’s definitely a problem. Is that what you mean?
